issues.legal_issue: The alternative method of proving a will through handwriting evidence is available only when the inability to produce an attesting witness is properly established.
material_facts: The will was attested by two witnesses; one had died, while the other was alive.
A summons was taken out for the living attesting witness but was not served.
No further summons or court process to compel the witness’s attendance was sought.
There was no evidence on oath establishing that the living witness was unavailable or had been kept away.
issues.conclusion: The requirements for using the alternative method of proof were not established, so the will could not be proved by that method on these facts. The appellate courts’ contrary approach was legally erroneous.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 68 and 69 of the Evidence Act, read with Section 63 of the Indian Succession Act, ordinarily require proof of a will through an attesting witness. The alternative method applies when no attesting witness can be found, including where a witness is dead, outside the court’s jurisdiction, kept away, or cannot be traced despite diligent search; the handwriting of the executant and at least one attesting witness must then be proved. The party must take appropriate steps to secure the witness, including available court process, before relying on that alternative. The Court relied on Hare Krishna Panigrahi v. Jogneswar Panda, Amal Sankar Sen v. The Dacca Co-operative Housing Society Ltd., and Doraiswami v. Rathnammal.

rule.if: will_proof_proceeding and one_attesting_witness_dead and other_attesting_witness_alive and summons_unserved and no_steps_to_compel_live_attestor and no_sworn_evidence_of_unavailability

predicates.will_proof_proceeding: A party sought to establish a will in a proceeding where proof of the will was required.
predicates.one_attesting_witness_dead: One of the will’s attesting witnesses had died.
predicates.summons_unserved: A summons for the living attesting witness was not served.
predicates.no_steps_to_compel_live_attestor: The party took no further steps to use court process to compel the living attesting witness to attend.
predicates.no_sworn_evidence_of_unavailability: No witness gave evidence on oath establishing that the living attesting witness could not be produced.

issues.definition: When a will is being proved, one attesting witness has died, and the living witness remains unproduced without effective steps to secure attendance or sworn evidence of unavailability, the alternative method of proof cannot be used.

issues.legal_issue: A statement by counsel across the bar cannot establish that an attesting witness is unavailable for the purpose of proving a will by an alternative method.
material_facts: The living attesting witness was not examined.
The assertion that the witness had gone abroad or had been won over was made by counsel, rather than established by the propounder’s sworn evidence.
The propounder did not give evidence on oath that the witness was unavailable.
issues.conclusion: The statements made by counsel, or otherwise made across the bar without being given in evidence on oath, could not establish the witness’s unavailability or justify resort to the alternative method of proof.
issues.legal_principle: For the alternative method of proving a will to be available, the inability to produce an attesting witness must be established by evidence; a statement across the bar is not a substitute for a witness’s deposition on oath. The Court relied on Hare Krishna Panigrahi v. Jogneswar Panda and Amal Sankar Sen v. The Dacca Co-operative Housing Society Ltd., and applied Sections 68 and 69 of the Evidence Act.

predicates.will_proof_proceeding: A party sought to establish a will in a proceeding where proof of the will was required.
predicates.counsel_asserted_attestor_unavailability: Counsel asserted that an attesting witness was unavailable.
predicates.no_sworn_testimony_supporting_unavailabi: No witness gave evidence on oath supporting the assertion that the attesting witness was unavailable.

issues.definition: When counsel asserts that an attesting witness is unavailable but no sworn testimony supports that assertion, the assertion does not establish unavailability.
